_comment: Equipment code -> what is actually in the cabin. This table exists because a feed giving an equipment code has NOT told you the cabin: hard rule 2 in table form. Amadeus returns aircraft.code ('789'), which names a TYPE. One carrier's 789 may be two or three configurations with two or three connectivity systems, and the frame is swapped after booking anyway. So every row here is a HEDGED CLAIM with an observed frequency, never a fact, and a type with no row still abstains rather than being guessed from the type alone.
_review: DRAFT - NOT human-reviewed. Every row carries needs_primary_source:true, the scorer prices it, and coverage() reports how many claims came from an unreviewed row. Before this is trusted in front of a user, each row needs a primary source (the carrier's own fleet page, or observed tail numbers by flight number) and needs_primary_source dropped. Treat the frequencies as the right SHAPE at roughly the right magnitude, not as measurements.
_keying: CARRIER:EQUIPMENT, on the OPERATING carrier - the metal belongs to whoever flies it, not to whoever sold it.
